hints.title: Earliest Positive Date
hints.text: Locate the earliest positive test date for each patient using group aggregation with minimum date.

hints.title: Subsequent Negative Match
hints.text: Join subsequent negative tests occurring strictly after the initial positive diagnosis date.

hints.title: Date Difference Calculation
hints.text: Compute the difference in days between the first negative recovery test and the initial positive test.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH first_positive AS (
    SELECT 
        patient_id,
        MIN(test_date) AS pos_date
    FROM covid_tests
    WHERE result = 'Positive'
    GROUP BY patient_id
),
first_subsequent_negative AS (
    SELECT 
        fp.patient_id,
        fp.pos_date,
        MIN(ct.test_date) AS neg_date
    FROM first_positive fp
    JOIN covid_tests ct ON fp.patient_id = ct.patient_id
    WHERE ct.result = 'Negative' AND ct.test_date > fp.pos_date
    GROUP BY fp.patient_id, fp.pos_date
)
SELECT 
    p.patient_id,
    p.patient_name,
    p.age,
    DATEDIFF(fn.neg_date, fn.pos_date) AS recovery_days
FROM first_subsequent_negative fn
JOIN patients p ON fn.patient_id = p.patient_id
ORDER BY recovery_days ASC, p.patient_id ASC;
```

variables: T: count of covid test records
complexity.notes: Two-stage group aggregation followed by date difference calculation and patient details join.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Cross-joining all tests without date filtering creates quadratic intermediate tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Aggregating minimum dates in CTEs prunes redundant intermediate tests.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use common table expressions to filter earliest positive and subsequent negative test dates.

WITH first_positive AS (
    SELECT 
        patient_id,
        MIN(test_date) AS pos_date
    FROM covid_tests
    WHERE result = 'Positive'
    GROUP BY patient_id
),
first_subsequent_negative AS (
    SELECT 
        fp.patient_id,
        fp.pos_date,
        MIN(ct.test_date) AS neg_date
    FROM first_positive fp
    JOIN covid_tests ct ON fp.patient_id = ct.patient_id
    WHERE ct.result = 'Negative' AND ct.test_date > fp.pos_date
    GROUP BY fp.patient_id, fp.pos_date
)
SELECT 
    p.patient_id,
    p.patient_name,
    p.age,
    (fn.neg_date - fn.pos_date) AS recovery_days
FROM first_subsequent_negative fn
JOIN patients p ON fn.patient_id = p.patient_id
ORDER BY recovery_days ASC, p.patient_id ASC;

import pandas as pd

def find_covid_recovery_patients(patients: pd.DataFrame, covid_tests: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    positives = covid_tests[covid_tests['result'] == 'Positive']
    first_pos = positives.groupby('patient_id')['test_date'].min().reset_index(name='pos_date')
    
    negatives = covid_tests[covid_tests['result'] == 'Negative']
    merged_tests = first_pos.merge(negatives, on='patient_id', how='inner')
    subsequent_neg = merged_tests[merged_tests['test_date'] > merged_tests['pos_date']]
    
    first_neg = subsequent_neg.groupby(['patient_id', 'pos_date'])['test_date'].min().reset_index(name='neg_date')
    first_neg['recovery_days'] = (pd.to_datetime(first_neg['neg_date']) - pd.to_datetime(first_neg['pos_date'])).dt.days
    
    res = first_neg.merge(patients, on='patient_id', how='inner')
    res = res.sort_values(by=['recovery_days', 'patient_id'], ascending=[True, True])
    return res[['patient_id', 'patient_name', 'age', 'recovery_days']]
